questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.solution:
The SI unit of force is the newton (N); $1\,\text{N} = 1\,\text{kg} \cdot \text{m/s}^2$.
Joule measures energy, watt measures power and pascal measures pressure.
**Answer: Newton**
questions.shortcut: F = ma gives kg·m/s², which is named the newton.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of washing soda?
questions.solution:
Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, $Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O$.
Baking soda is NaHCO₃, caustic soda is NaOH and bleaching powder is CaOCl₂.
**Answer: Na₂CO₃·10H₂O**
questions.shortcut: Washing = carbonate + 10 waters; baking = bicarbonate (NaHCO₃).

questions.q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes night blindness?
questions.solution:
Night blindness (poor vision in dim light) is caused by a deficiency of vitamin A, which the body makes from carotene present in carrots, papaya, etc.
**Answer: Vitamin A**
questions.shortcut: A for 'Aankh' (eye): vitamin A → night blindness.

questions.q: Which type of lens is used to correct myopia (short-sightedness)?
questions.solution:
In myopia the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina.
A concave (diverging) lens pushes the image back onto the retina.
**Answer: Concave lens**
questions.shortcut: Myopia–minus–concave; hypermetropia–plus–convex.

questions.q: Which gas is commonly known as 'laughing gas'?
questions.solution:
Nitrous oxide ($N_2O$), used as a mild anaesthetic, is called laughing gas.
Nitric oxide is NO, carbon monoxide is the poisonous gas CO and SO₂ causes acid rain.
**Answer: Nitrous oxide**
questions.shortcut: Laughing = N₂O = nitrous oxide.

questions.q: Which cell organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.solution:
Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration and release energy stored as ATP, hence the name 'powerhouse of the cell'.
**Answer: Mitochondria**
questions.shortcut: Power → ATP → mitochondria.

questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
questions.solution:
Light travels at about $3 \times 10^8$ m/s (3,00,000 km/s) in vacuum — the fastest speed in the universe.
**Answer: 3 × 10⁸ m/s**

questions.q: What is the pH value of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.solution:
Pure water is neutral: its pH is 7 at 25 °C.
Below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic.
**Answer: 7**
questions.shortcut: Neutral = 7 on the pH scale.

questions.q: Which blood cells help the body to fight infection?
questions.solution:
White blood cells (WBCs or leucocytes) defend the body against infection.
RBCs carry oxygen and platelets help in clotting.
**Answer: WBC**
questions.shortcut: W = Warrior cells: WBCs fight germs.

questions.q: Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.solution:
A convex mirror always gives an erect, diminished (virtual) image and a much wider field of view, which is why it is used as a rear-view mirror.
**Answer: Convex mirror**
questions.shortcut: Wide view needed behind → convex mirror.

questions.q: Which is the lightest element?
questions.solution:
Hydrogen (atomic number 1, atomic mass about 1) is the lightest element and the most abundant element in the universe.
**Answer: Hydrogen**
questions.shortcut: First on the periodic table = lightest = hydrogen.

questions.q: Which is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.solution:
The skin is the largest organ of the human body.
(The liver is the largest internal organ/gland.)
**Answer: Skin**
questions.shortcut: Skin covers the whole body — the largest organ; liver is the largest internal one.

questions.q: An electric bulb rated 100 W is used for 5 hours in a day. How much electrical energy does it consume in that day?
questions.solution:
Energy = Power × time $= 0.1\,\text{kW} \times 5\,\text{h} = 0.5$ kWh (0.5 unit).
**Answer: 0.5 kWh**
questions.shortcut: kWh = kilowatts × hours: 0.1 × 5 = 0.5.

questions.q: Rusting of iron takes place only in the presence of:
questions.solution:
Iron rusts when both oxygen (from air) and moisture (water) act on it; either one alone is not enough.
Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide.
**Answer: Oxygen and moisture**
questions.shortcut: Rust needs air AND water together.

questions.q: During photosynthesis, green plants release which gas?
questions.solution:
In photosynthesis plants take in carbon dioxide and water and release oxygen:
$6CO_2 + 6H_2O \to C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2$ (in sunlight, with chlorophyll).
**Answer: Oxygen**
questions.shortcut: Plants breathe out O₂ in the day: CO₂ in, O₂ out.

questions.q: At which temperature (in °C) does water have maximum density?
questions.solution:
Water shows anomalous expansion: its density is maximum (1 g/cm³) at 4 °C.
This is why ice floats and aquatic life survives under a frozen lake.
**Answer: 4 °C**
questions.shortcut: Water's odd behaviour: densest at 4 °C, not at 0 °C.

questions.q: Which acid is present in lemon?
questions.solution:
Lemon and other citrus fruits contain citric acid.
Vinegar has acetic acid, curd has lactic acid and tamarind has tartaric acid.
**Answer: Citric acid**
questions.shortcut: Citrus → citric acid.

questions.q: Malaria is spread by the bite of which mosquito?
questions.solution:
Malaria is transmitted by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito carrying the Plasmodium parasite.
The Aedes mosquito spreads dengue and chikungunya.
**Answer: Female Anopheles mosquito**
questions.shortcut: Malaria = female Anopheles; dengue = Aedes.

questions.q: Sound CANNOT travel through:
questions.solution:
Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium to travel.
It cannot travel through vacuum, although light can.
**Answer: Vacuum**
questions.shortcut: No medium, no sound: vacuum kills sound waves.

questions.q: Which gas is released when baking soda reacts with vinegar?
questions.solution:
Baking soda (sodium hydrogen carbonate) reacts with the acetic acid in vinegar to give carbon dioxide gas — this causes the fizz.
**Answer: Carbon dioxide**
questions.shortcut: Acid + carbonate/bicarbonate → CO₂ always.

questions.q: What is the normal temperature of the human body?
questions.solution:
The normal temperature of the human body is about 37 °C (98.6 °F).
**Answer: 37 °C**
questions.shortcut: 37 °C = 98.6 °F — memorise the pair.

questions.q: A fruit detaches from a tree and falls to the ground because of which force?
questions.solution:
The Earth pulls every object towards itself by the force of gravity — the same force Newton associated with a falling apple.
**Answer: Gravitational force**
questions.shortcut: Falling towards the Earth = gravity.

questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.solution:
Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature; it is used in thermometers.
(Bromine is a liquid too, but it is a non-metal.)
**Answer: Mercury**
questions.shortcut: Liquid metal = mercury (Hg).

questions.q: Insulin, which controls the blood sugar level, is produced by which organ?
questions.solution:
Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas; it lowers blood sugar.
Its deficiency causes diabetes.
**Answer: Pancreas**
questions.shortcut: Insulin → pancreas; thyroxine → thyroid.

questions.q: Which part of the plant is the main site of photosynthesis?
questions.solution:
Leaves contain chlorophyll and are called the 'food factories' of the plant — the main site of photosynthesis.
**Answer: Leaf**
questions.shortcut: Green, broad, chlorophyll-rich = leaf = food factory.

questions.q: In which year was the Quit India Movement launched?
questions.solution:
The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 with the call of 'Do or Die'.
**Answer: 1942**
questions.shortcut: Quit India = 1942; Non-cooperation = 1920; Civil Disobedience/Dandi = 1930.

questions.q: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
questions.solution:
Chandragupta Maurya, guided by his minister Chanakya (Kautilya), founded the Maurya Empire around 322 BC.
Bindusara was his son and Ashoka his grandson.
**Answer: Chandragupta Maurya**
questions.shortcut: Founder Chandragupta I, chanakya the guide; Ashoka came two generations later.

questions.q: In which city did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919 take place?
questions.solution:
On 13 April 1919, troops under General Dyer fired on an unarmed gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, Punjab.
**Answer: Amritsar**
questions.shortcut: Jallianwala Bagh is in Amritsar (Baisakhi day, 1919).

questions.q: How many Fundamental Rights are guaranteed by the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The Constitution guarantees six Fundamental Rights (Articles 12–35): equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and constitutional remedies.
The right to property was removed from this list by the 44th Amendment (1978).
**Answer: Six**
questions.shortcut: After 1978 it is 6 — property right became a legal right.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?
questions.solution:
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution and is called the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.
**Answer: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**
questions.shortcut: Drafting Committee chairman = Ambedkar.

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
Odisha is not among them.
**Answer: Odisha**
questions.shortcut: Remember the 8-state list; Odisha and Bihar are the common traps.

questions.q: The Sundarbans, the largest delta in the world, is formed by the Ganga and which other river?
questions.solution:
The Sundarbans delta (West Bengal–Bangladesh) is formed by the Ganga and the Brahmaputra (with the Meghna).
**Answer: Brahmaputra**
questions.shortcut: Ganga + Brahmaputra = Sundarbans delta.

questions.q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.solution:
The Kosi, which frequently changes course and floods north Bihar, is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.
The Damodar is the 'Sorrow of Bengal'.
**Answer: Kosi**
questions.shortcut: Kosi–Bihar, Damodar–Bengal: keep the pair straight.

questions.q: NITI Aayog replaced which of the following bodies?
questions.solution:
NITI Aayog, set up on 1 January 2015, replaced the Planning Commission (established in 1950).
**Answer: Planning Commission**
questions.shortcut: 2015: Planning Commission → NITI Aayog.

questions.q: Bharatanatyam, a major classical dance form, originates from which state?
questions.solution:
Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu.
Kathakali belongs to Kerala, Kuchipudi to Andhra Pradesh and Kathak to north India.
**Answer: Tamil Nadu**
questions.shortcut: Bharatanatyam–Tamil Nadu, Kathakali–Kerala, Kuchipudi–Andhra.

questions.q: The Duleep Trophy is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
The Duleep Trophy is a premier domestic first-class cricket tournament in India, played by zonal teams.
**Answer: Cricket**
questions.shortcut: Ranji, Duleep, Irani — all first-class cricket trophies.

questions.q: Who wrote the book 'The Discovery of India'?
questions.solution:
'The Discovery of India' (1946) was written by Jawaharlal Nehru during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort.
'My Experiments with Truth' is Gandhiji's autobiography.
**Answer: Jawaharlal Nehru**
questions.shortcut: Nehru wrote Discovery of India and Glimpses of World History.

questions.q: The Hirakud Dam is built on which river?
questions.solution:
The Hirakud Dam, one of the longest dams in the world, is built across the Mahanadi near Sambalpur in Odisha.
**Answer: Mahanadi**
questions.shortcut: Hirakud–Mahanadi–Odisha: fix the triple.

questions.q: Major Dhyan Chand, whose birth anniversary is celebrated as National Sports Day, was associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
Major Dhyan Chand, the legendary centre-forward who won three Olympic gold medals in hockey, is honoured on National Sports Day (29 August).
**Answer: Hockey**
questions.shortcut: The hockey wizard — Dhyan Chand = hockey.

questions.q: Which city is known as the 'Pink City' of India?
questions.solution:
Jaipur, founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II, is called the Pink City for the pink colour of its old-city buildings.
**Answer: Jaipur**
questions.shortcut: Pink City = Jaipur; Blue City = Jodhpur.

questions.q: Which team won the ICC Champions Trophy 2025?
questions.solution:
India won the ICC Champions Trophy 2025, defeating New Zealand by 4 wickets in the final at Dubai on 9 March 2025 — India's third Champions Trophy title (2002 shared, 2013, 2025).
**Answer: India**
questions.shortcut: 2025 CT final: India beat New Zealand in Dubai.

questions.q: In which country were the 2026 Winter Olympics held?
questions.solution:
The 2026 Winter Olympics were held in Milan–Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy, in February 2026.
**Answer: Italy**
questions.shortcut: 2026 Winter Games = Milan–Cortina, Italy.

questions.q: The FIFA World Cup 2026 was hosted jointly by which three countries?
questions.solution:
The FIFA World Cup 2026 was jointly hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico — the first three-nation World Cup, expanded to 48 teams.
**Answer: USA, Canada and Mexico**
questions.shortcut: 2026 WC hosts: USA + Canada + Mexico (48 teams).

questions.q: Who became the first Indian to travel to the International Space Station (Axiom-4 mission, June 2025)?
questions.solution:
Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla became the first Indian to visit the International Space Station, serving as pilot of the private Axiom-4 mission in June 2025.
Rakesh Sharma (1984) was the first Indian in space, aboard the Salyut 7 station.
**Answer: Shubhanshu Shukla**
questions.shortcut: First Indian in space: Rakesh Sharma (1984); first Indian on the ISS: Shubhanshu Shukla (2025).

questions.q: Who took oath as the 52nd Chief Justice of India in May 2025?
questions.solution:
Justice B.R. Gavai took oath as the 52nd Chief Justice of India on 14 May 2025, succeeding Justice Sanjiv Khanna.
**Answer: Justice B.R. Gavai**
questions.shortcut: May 2025: Khanna → Gavai (52nd CJI).
